i0: ***Some*** and ***any*** talk about an amount that isn't exact. Use them with **plural** nouns (*some eggs*) and **uncountable** nouns (*some milk*).
i1: The basic rule is ***some*** in positive sentences and ***any*** in negatives and questions, but there are important exceptions. For countable and uncountable nouns, see [Countable and Uncountable Nouns](/blog/grammar/countable-uncountable-nouns/).
sa-basic.t: Some in positive sentences, any in negatives and questions
sa-basic.s: Use ***some*** in **positive** sentences (*I've got some apples*). Use ***any*** in **negatives** (*I haven't got any apples*) and most **questions** (*Have you got any apples?*).
sa-basic.b1: Use *some / any* with **plural** and **uncountable** nouns. With a singular countable noun, use *a / an*: *Is there **a** bank near here?* (not *any bank*)
sa-offers.t: Some in offers and requests: Can I have some water?
sa-offers.s: Use ***some*** in **questions** when you **offer** something or **ask for** something, or when you expect the answer *yes*: *Would you like **some** coffee? Can I have **some** water?*
sa-offers.b0.1.1: *Can I have **some** water, please? Could you lend me **some** money?*
sa-offers.b0.2.1: *Did you buy **some** bread?* (I think you did.)
sa-offers.b1: Compare: *Have you got **any** questions?* (an open question) / *Would you like **some** more tea?* (an offer).
sa-compounds.s: ***Some-, any-, no-, every-*** combine with ***-one / -body*** (people), ***-thing*** (things) and ***-where*** (places): *someone, anything, nowhere, everybody*. Use them like *some* and *any*.
sa-compounds.b1: ***No-*** words already have a negative meaning, so use a **positive** verb: *I saw **nobody**.* = *I didn't see **anybody**.* (not *I didn't see nobody*)
sa-compounds.b2: These words take a **singular** verb: ***Everyone is** here. **Nothing has** changed.*
sa-compounds.b3: Don't use *to* before *somewhere / anywhere* after *go*: *Let's go **somewhere** quiet.*
sa-any-meaning.t: Any = it doesn't matter which; any after if
sa-any-meaning.s: In **positive** sentences, ***any*** means **it doesn't matter which**: *Call me **any** time.* Use ***any*** after ***if*** and with words that have a **negative meaning** (*never, hardly, without*).
sa-any-meaning.b0.0.1: *Choose **any** colour you like. **Anyone** can learn to cook.*
sa-any-meaning.b1: With this meaning, *any* can go with a **singular** noun: ***Any** child can do it. Take **any** bus from here.*
sa-any-meaning.b2: ***Not… any*** = ***no***: *There **aren't any** chairs.* = *There **are no** chairs.* Use only **one** negative.
x.sa-compounds-s02: No-word with a positive verb: *There's nothing*.
